newsitem.title: USA: CBOT to stand by corn/soybean delivery proposal.
newsitem.headline: CBOT to stand by corn/soybean delivery proposal.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade said Monday it stood by proposed changes to its corn and soybean futures delivery system in the face of plans by several U.S. lawmakers to ask this week for a Justice Department probe.

"Our response is what we've been saying all along, and that is that the (exchange's) task force did a thorough and thoughtful analysis of the grain delivery system and came up with the best possible plan," a CBOT spokesman said.
"Our membership approved it overwhelmingly and we continue to stand by it," the spokesman said.

Congressional staffers in Washington on Friday said several lawmakers planned to ask the Justice Department this week to review the CBOT's plan to change its delivery locations for corn and soybean futures.
"The proposal by the CBOT has the potential to severely impede competition and increase market manipulation," a draft letter from the lawmakers to Attorney General Janet Reno said.

The draft letter was released by the office of Ohio Democratic Representative Marcy Kaptur, who has been a force in the House behind pursuing official review of the CBOT plan along with Michigan Democrat John Dingell.

The proposal, approved by the CBOT membership in April by a 2-to-1 majority, would eliminate delivery points in Toledo, Ohio, and St. Louis, Missouri. It would allow delivery along the Illinois River from Pekin, Illinois, to Chicago, including Burns Harbor, Indiana.
The plan was created by a CBOT Task Force made up of grain industry officials, traders and academic specialists.

But the plan has drawn fire from politicians, farm groups and grain elevators. Dozens of opponents have sent letters to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which must approve the plan before it can take effect.
"The proposal would result in highly concentrated ownership of delivery elevators among a small number of commercial grain companies along the Illinois River," the draft letter said.
But the CBOT spokesman said, "There is no legal reason for the CFTC to reject the CBOT's balanced proposal."
The CFTC has scheduled a public hearing on June 12 to hear additional views on the plan.
